cards.text: About that time, King Herod reaches out to harm some who belong to the church. He has James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword. Friend, this one starts heavy.

cards.question: Herod sees that killing James pleased the Jews. So what does Herod do next?

cards.text: So Herod has Peter, one of Jesus' twelve apostles (Matthew 10:2), arrested during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
Peter goes into prison, guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Friend, that's SIXTEEN soldiers for ONE man, and NOBODY ever guarded my cookie jar like that.

cards.question: Herod intends to bring Peter out to the people after the ___.
True or false: While Peter is kept in prison, the church is fervently praying to God for him.

cards.text: It's the night before Herod is set to bring Peter to trial. Sentries are standing guard at the entrance to the prison.

cards.question: On the night before his trial, Peter is ___ between two soldiers.

cards.text: Two soldiers, two chains, a trial in the morning, and the man is SLEEPING. Friend, I can't fall asleep if I'm not sure I turned the oven off!
Suddenly an angel of the Lord appears, and a light shines in the cell.

cards.question: The angel needs Peter awake. How does the angel wake him up?

answers.text: He taps Peter on the side
He shakes Peter by the shoulders

cards.question: The angel tells Peter, “Get up quickly.” True or false: Peter's chains fall off his wrists.

cards.text: Then the angel tells Peter to get dressed, put on his sandals, wrap his cloak around him and follow. Even in a prison break, friend, you put your shoes on first.

cards.question: Peter follows the angel out, but he doesn't realize it's real. What does Peter think is happening?

answers.text: The guards are setting a trap
Herod has decided to free him

cards.text: His chains just hit the floor and he thinks it's a vision. Honestly, friend, if my chains fell off in the middle of the night, I'd roll over and hit SNOOZE.

cards.question: Peter and the angel pass the first and second guards and reach the iron gate leading to the city. What happens at the gate?

answers.text: It opens for them by itself
The angel breaks the lock off
A guard unlocks it for them

cards.question: True or false: Once they're out in the city, the angel walks Peter all the way to a friend's house.
Standing alone in the street, Peter comes to himself. What does Peter now know for sure?

answers.text: The Lord sent His angel to rescue him
The guards let him go on purpose
Herod changed his mind about him

cards.text: Once it sinks in, Peter goes to the house of Mary, the mother of John, also called Mark. Many people have gathered there, and they're praying.
Peter knocks at the outer gate, and a servant girl named Rhoda comes to answer it.

cards.question: Rhoda recognizes Peter's voice at the gate, and she's overjoyed. What does she do?

answers.text: Runs inside and leaves the gate shut
Throws the gate wide open for him
Faints right there at the gate

cards.text: She runs inside and announces, “Peter is standing at the gate!” Friend, that's like yelling that the cookies are done and leaving them IN THE OVEN.

cards.question: True or false: The people praying at Mary's house believe Rhoda right away.

cards.text: “You are out of your mind,” they tell her, and when she keeps insisting, they say, “It must be his angel.” Friend, they prayed for this EXACT thing, and when it shows up knocking, they're inside arguing about it!

cards.question: Peter keeps on knocking. When they finally open the door and see him, they are ___.

cards.text: Peter motions with his hand for silence and describes how the Lord brought him out of the prison. “Send word to James and to the brothers,” he tells them.

cards.question: True or false: The James that Peter sends word to is the same James that Herod put to death.
Once Peter gives his message about James and the brothers, what does Peter do?

answers.text: He stays the night at Mary's
He goes back to face Herod

cards.text: At daybreak there's no small commotion among the soldiers about what became of Peter. Sixteen soldiers, one empty cell, and I bet NOT ONE of them wants to be the guy who tells Herod.

cards.question: Herod searches for Peter and can't find him. After he examines the guards, what does Herod order?

answers.text: That the guards be locked up
That the guards be sent home

cards.text: Then Herod goes down from Judea to Caesarea and spends some time there. Now he's in a furious dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon, so they win the support of Blastus, the king's chamberlain, and ask for peace.

cards.question: Tyre and Sidon ask for peace because their region depends on the king's country for ___.
On the appointed day, Herod puts on his royal robes, sits on his throne and speaks to the people. What do they shout his voice is?

answers.text: The voice of a true king

cards.question: Immediately, an angel of the Lord strikes Herod down, because he did not give ___ to God.

cards.text: Herod is eaten by worms and dies. The king who reached out to harm the church is gone, but the word of God keeps spreading and multiplying.

cards.question: Barnabas and Saul had carried the disciples' gifts to the elders in Judea (Acts 11:29-30). When they finish their mission to Jerusalem and head back, who do they bring with them?

findings.problem: The passage opens mid-thought with "About that time," which points back to Acts 11. The opening card repeats the phrase but never says what time it was or what was going on.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Peter first appears in this card's right answer, but he isn't identified until card 3.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He apologizes to the church" doesn't fit a king who has just had James killed. It reads as silly and is easy to rule out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This card adds no new part of the passage. It only restates the chains and the vision, then makes a joke. The joke also fails the logic test. Peter thinks the rescue isn't real, but hitting snooze means ignoring an alarm, not doubting what's real. Papa Dorin never had chains either.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card tells about the chains falling off (Acts 12:7), but it cites only Acts 12:9.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "They prayed for this EXACT thing" goes beyond the text. Acts 12:5 says the church was praying to God "for him," and Acts 12:12 says only that they were praying. Neither says they prayed for his release. The card also draws on Acts 12:5 and 12:12 but cites only Acts 12:15.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: A new James first appears in Peter's message, but the card never says who he is. That matters because the very next card asks whether he is the James Herod killed.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This card holds more than two beats. Herod moves to Caesarea, he is in a dispute with Tyre and Sidon, and they win Blastus's support and ask for peace.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: "The king who reached out to harm the church" draws on Acts 12:1, but the card cites only Acts 12:23-24.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Barnabas and Saul appear here for the first time in the passage, but the card doesn't say who they are. It only mentions their errand from Acts 11.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
